title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding notes): X is a space stratified by a poset I. The X_i are the closed strata, and X_i^* = X_i minus the union of the X_j with j<i is the open stratum. Each X_i has a tubular neighbourhood T_i with boundary \dot T_i ('sphere bundle' boundary). δ(i) is a dimension or depth index. X^{(d)} is a 'deployed' (unfolded) piece of X, presumably X with the open tubes around lower strata removed.

On this page Grothendieck defines the pieces of the déploiement.

1. Deployed strata. Σ_i = X_i^{(d)} = X_i ∩ X^{(d)} with d = δ(i). This is the compact 'manifold with boundary/corners' model of the open stratum X_i^*.

2. Link pieces, for i<j (49). Σ_ij = \dot T_i ∩ Σ_j ⊂ Σ_j. This is the part of the boundary of the tube around X_i lying in the deployed stratum Σ_j, a boundary face of Σ_j.

3. Flags (50). For a flag i_0<...<i_n:
- Σ_{i_0...i_n} = \dot T_{i_0} ∩ ... ∩ \dot T_{i_{n-1}} ∩ Σ_{i_n}.
- Equivalently, Σ_{i_0...i_n} = ∩_k Σ_{i_k i_n}.
- These are the corner strata of Σ_{i_n}, models for iterated (generalized) links.

4. Functoriality. These pieces form a diagram over the flags of I, i.e. over the barycentric subdivision sd(I).
- For the 'canonical' flag inclusions, i.e. dropping indices other than the last one i_n, there are obvious transition maps. These are inclusions of intersections.
- For arbitrary face inclusions (dropping the top index) the maps depend on choosing retractions T_i^{(d)} → X_i^{(d)} = Σ_i.
- This yields Σ_ij ⊂ \dot T_i^{(d)} ⊂ T_i^{(d)} → Σ_i.
- Hence the 'complete structure': the family (Σ_i), the family (Σ_ij), the inclusions Σ_ij → Σ_j and the projections Σ_ij → Σ_i.

5. Hypotheses. For the projections Σ_ij → Σ_i to be fibrations one needs two things:
- an equisingularity / local triviality hypothesis on the stratification;
- a compatibility condition on the retractions, of the kind satisfied by commuting Thom–Mather control data.

Purpose: reduce a (tame) stratified space to a combinatorial system of manifolds with corners and fibrations indexed by flags of the stratification poset, from which X is recovered by gluing. The next page replaces the choice-dependent tubes by canonical pro-neighbourhoods ('procespaces') 𝒱_i, 𝒱_{i_0...i_n} = ∩𝒱_{i_k}, which are strictly functorial. There X = colim of the 𝒱_i glued along the 𝒱_ij.
errors: Not a real error: the second equality in (50) holds by idempotence of intersection, since Σ_{i_k i_n} = \dot T_{i_k} ∩ Σ_{i_n} for each k.
Gap: the map Σ_ij → Σ_i requires Σ_ij ⊂ T_i^{(d)} with d = δ(i), i.e. Σ_j ⊂ X^{(δ(i))}. This compatibility between the X^{(d)} for different d is implicit and not stated.

Gap: the conditions making Σ_ij → Σ_i fibrations are only gestured at ('hyp. d'équisingularité...', 'une condition sur les rétractions'). The needed commutation of retractions (π_i∘π_j = π_i on overlaps, as in Mather's control data) is not formulated. The expression '√T^{(d)}_{(d)} → X^{(d)}_{(d)}' is cryptic.

ideas.what: Deployment (unfolding) of a stratified space into compact manifolds with corners Σ_i (strata minus open tubes of lower strata), with boundary faces Σ_ij fibred over Σ_i
ideas.modern_name: Resolution / unfolding / 'unzipping' of a Thom–Mather (Whitney) stratified space into manifolds with corners; abstract stratified spaces as systems of manifolds with fibred boundary faces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970/2012) control data; Verona (1984); Melrose and others (iterated fibration structures, resolution of stratified spaces); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping, 2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6 on tame topology / 'dévissage' of stratified structures (described there in outline, without these formulas)

ideas.what: Iterated link pieces Σ_{i_0...i_n} indexed by flags of the stratification poset, forming a diagram over sd(I): strict for flag inclusions keeping the top element, choice-dependent (retractions) for the others
ideas.modern_name: Generalized homotopy links / diagrams over the subdivision sd(P) (stratified homotopy hypothesis); exit-path data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); Miller (2013); Douteau, Haine, Douteau–Waas (diagrams over sd(P), 2018–2021); Lurie HA A.6 (exit paths)

ideas.what: Fibration conditions for the projections Σ_ij → Σ_i require local triviality (equisingularity) plus compatibility of tubular retractions
ideas.modern_name: Commuting tubular projections / control data; Thom's first isotopy lemma

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly organizes the deployed pieces as a diagram indexed by flags of the stratification poset (i.e. sd(I)). He notes that the face maps preserving the top element are strict inclusions, while the others need non-canonical retractions. This is exactly the shape of the later Douteau–Waas / Haine description of stratified homotopy types as diagrams over sd(P). It anticipates the strictification problem that motivates using homotopy links, or here pro-neighbourhoods (next page).
missed.quote: On a de façon évidente les morphismes de transition entre les Σ_{i0…in} pour les inclusions canoniques de drapeaux, mais non pour des inclusions quelconques, dont la définition dépend des choix de rétractions
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck reaching (c. 1981–82) the sd(P)-diagram model of stratified spaces decades before its formalization. His pro-space ('procespace') strictification on the next page is an alternative to Quinn's homotopy links. As far as I know it is not explored in the current stratified homotopy literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The deployment into manifolds with corners is in the spirit of Thom–Mather/Verona and is sketched in the Esquisse. The explicit flag-indexed (sd(I)) organization, with the strict versus choice-dependent face maps distinguished, is a nice unpublished anticipation of modern diagram models of stratified homotopy theory. The page itself is a sketch, though.
transcription_corrections: 'pour une drapeau' should read 'pour un drapeau'.
First line: 'si i<j' followed by the struck-out '[d=δ(i), d'=δ(j)]'. In (49) the struck-out text before \dot T_i is an aborted start of 'T_i∩Σ_j'.
The 'structure complète' line in the image shows Σ_ij → Σ_j and Σ_ij → Σ_i drawn as two arrows from Σ_ij.
The reading 'hyp. d'équisingularité' is uncertain; the handwriting is ambiguous.
The phrase reads 'et une condition sur les rétractions T_i^{(d)} → X_i', with 'sur les' inserted above the line.
